BUG: Loop restart re-drives the whole signal file (offset/notified live only in memory), so one pending wake appends a byte-identical second notice to wakeups.jsonl; any consumer that counts notices can double-dispatch
MINIMAL_FIX: Make the wake notice idempotent across restarts with the smallest in-place change, e.g. persist the loop offset (+ last notified triple) beside the Kirby state file and reload it at startup, or have _notice() skip when the file tail already holds the identical (session_id, workkey, token) triple. Pin with a test: two run_once passes with a fresh state dict over the same signal file produce exactly one wakeups.jsonl line.
RAW_EVIDENCE: courier_runtime/host_loop.py run_once(): state={offset,last_tick,notified} is passed in-memory (main() builds it fresh each start); a missing/truncated file resets offset to 0 and old IDLE lines re-drive wake()->deliver path; _notice() dedupes only against the in-memory triple, so a restart appends the identical notice again. Probe /tmp/probe_p3_hostloop.py: run1 1 notice, restarted run2 (fresh state) results ['COALESCED'] yet appends a 2nd identical line -> DUPLICATE_NOTICE=True. Fencing tokens correctly prevent double EXECUTION (second pass coalesces), so the defect is confined to the notice channel, which is exactly the duplicate-effect surface.
REPRO_STEPS: 1. Kirby + signal file with one IDLE line; run_once -> 1 notice. 2. Rebuild Kirby from the same state file with a fresh loop-state dict (simulating process restart). 3. run_once again -> results ['COALESCED'] (no double execution) but wakeups.jsonl now has 2 identical lines. See /tmp/probe_p3_hostloop.py.
TARGETED_TEST: Feed the same signal file to two consecutive run_once calls with fresh loop state and assert wakeups.jsonl holds exactly one notice for the (session_id, workkey, token) triple.
